text:
**Yes, some can, but not all.** A power station only works as a UPS if it has a documented automatic switchover (UPS or EPS mode) with a published transfer time. A basic unit may keep appliances running but still cut power to your computer for a moment during an outage ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups)).

**What to check**
- **Transfer time:** 10 ms is common on UPS-capable models, while some are 20-30 ms. EcoFlow says many units advertised as UPS are too slow, and that 30 ms or more can risk data corruption ([EcoFlow](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply)). That is a manufacturer's claim, so treat it with some caution.
- **It isn't 0 ms:** Anker notes that 10 or 20 ms is not the zero-gap switchover of an online double-conversion UPS. If your computer or NAS manual requires 0 ms, or you have a critical workload, buy an online UPS instead ([Anker SOLIX](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/home-power-backup/portable-power-station-ups-home-server-nas)). Check your computer's power supply specs against the station's published transfer time.
- **Pass-through use:** Confirm the manufacturer supports running the station continuously while it charges from the wall. Pass-through alone isn't UPS protection.
- **Output type and power:** Look for pure sine wave output. The station's continuous wattage should exceed your total load, and a plug-in watt meter will tell you what your setup actually draws.
- **Runtime:** Hours ≈ Wh × ~0.85 ÷ load in watts. A 1,000 Wh unit running a 100 W load gives about 8.5 hours at best, and real-world runtime will be shorter.
- **Shutdown signaling:** Most power stations don't tell your computer to shut down automatically the way a standard UPS can. EcoFlow lists UPS-HID support for some models, so check the specs if you want that.

**Options with a listed UPS switchover** (from [Dealectric's roundup](https://dealectric.com/answers/portable-power-station-ups-transfer-time-computer-manufacturer-guidance-ecoflow-). The buy links below are affiliate links, and Dealectric is paid if you buy):
- **[BLUETTI Elite 30 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-30-v2):** ≤10 ms, 288 Wh, 600 W. About $275.50 with code AFF5OFF. Suits a laptop or small setup, but the battery is small.
- **[ALLPOWERS P1800](https://dealectric.com/go/allpowers-p1800-1024wh):** ≤10 ms, 1,024 Wh, 1,800 W. About $395.10 with code ALLPOWERS26. Its store page contradicts itself on some specs (the product images say 15 ms), so verify before buying.
- **[BLUETTI Elite 200 V2](https://dealectric.com/go/bluetti-elite-200-v2):** ≤15 ms, 2,073.6 Wh, 2,600 W. About $854.05 with code AFF5OFF. Better for a computer plus a router and other gear.
- **[Anker SOLIX S2000](https://www.ankersolix.com/blogs/portable-power-station/can-a-portable-power-station-be-used-as-a-ups):** 10 ms switchover, 2,010 Wh, 1,500 W pure sine wave. $699.99 after coupon, per Anker's page.
- **EcoFlow RIVER 3 Plus:** <10 ms and 600 W, per [EcoFlow's blog](https://www.ecoflow.com/us/blog/use-portable-power-station-as-ups-power-supply). I didn't get a purchase link or price for it.

The BLUETTI AC180 and AC200L list 20 ms, so I'd skip them for a sensitive computer.

For a typical desktop or laptop, a 10 ms unit is a reasonable choice if your computer's power supply specs allow that gap. If you want to be conservative, or the data is critical, an online UPS is the safer pick, with a power station as longer-term backup.

If you tell me your computer's wattage, and whether you also need to power a monitor or router, I can narrow this down.
